title: A fixed second harmonic reduces held-season GJ 674 velocity error in five selected HARPS seasons
abstract: We test the second orbital harmonic of GJ 674 b in 224 public HARPS-RVBank version 02 exposures from five dense seasons. At a fixed 4.69507-day period, a harmonic fitted to the other four seasons reduces held-season weighted squared error by 10.9 to 37.6 percent. All 26 extraction, activity and baseline control settings keep positive point gains in all five seasons. Conditional common-coefficient sign tests give seasonal-change tail fractions from 0.370 to 0.672. However, all seasons have 30-day gain perturbation ranges that include zero. The result shows consistency under selected fits. It does not prove an eccentric orbit or distinguish it from two circular signals. The products share spectra. No independent instrument confirmation or new planet is found. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, a retrieval script, a figure and independent numerical checks are included. Raw data remain outside the signed bundle.

display.caption: Left: seasonal second-harmonic coefficient estimates and pooled fit. Right: held-season error gains with envelopes of conditional 30-day sign ranges. Every envelope includes zero. The envelopes are not calibrated confidence intervals.
